transcript.text: hey. i want to hit about 150g protein a day. not sure where to start

150g of protein a day? Let's go! I'm ZOH. I'll help you get better at this with one small step a day. Text "stop" anytime, and tell me if you want me to coach differently, like "chill out" or "push me harder." What's your name?
Good to meet you, Jordan. 150g is a solid target, and we'll build up to it one step at a time. What time of day works best for you to log your protein?
Jordan here. I eat around 8am, 1pm and 7pm, so i guess any of those. but i dont want to spend more than 5 min a day logging

Five minutes is plenty, Jordan. A set time is what makes it stick, so pick one: log right after your 7pm dinner and see the whole day at once, or after your 1pm lunch to check you're on pace. Which works better?
After dinner works. Do you already use an app to track what you eat, like MyFitnessPal, or would you start from scratch?
i use myfitnesspal on and off. kinda forget to open it lol
Ha, that's super common, and it's why we're tying it to dinner. Where do you want this to get you: a certain weight, more muscle, just feeling better? Totally fine if you're not sure yet.
just wanna hit 150g a day and stop forgetting lol. no specific weight thing

Forgetting to open the app is the real problem, Jordan, so the plan is built around fixing that. Here's the draft:

• Headed for: 150g protein a day, and no more forgetting to log
• Setup today: move MyFitnessPal to your home screen and set a 7:30 pm alarm labeled "log protein"
• Day 1, tonight at 7:30 pm: log everything from today (8am, 1pm and 7pm meals) and see your protein total. You don't have to hit 150 yet.
• Every day, 5 minutes, on your phone wherever you are
• Proof: a screenshot of your MyFitnessPal daily summary showing protein. If that's a pain, a voice note with your number works too.
• Why: a 5-minute log tied to dinner stops the forgetting, and your real number shows how far you are from 150g.

Each day's step builds from how the last one went, so we close the gap to 150g gradually. What do you think?
